paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me. God's Word is worth saying all the way through, even when you know the room won't clap. The LORD told Jeremiah, "Do not omit a word," and Jeremiah said all of it (Jeremiah 26:2, 8). Then the crowd grabbed him, and he still stood there and told them to "correct your ways and deeds, and obey the voice of the LORD your God" (Jeremiah 26:13).

Now notice WHY the LORD sent that hard message. He said, "Perhaps they will listen and turn," so that He might "relent of the disaster" (Jeremiah 26:3), and the warning was an open door, not a slammed one. The elders saw it when they remembered Micah, because Hezekiah feared the LORD and sought His favor, and the LORD relented (Jeremiah 26:19). When God warns you, friend, He is still giving you room to turn.

And then there's the part that sits heavy. Uriah said the same things and was put to the sword, while Jeremiah was spared because Ahikam son of Shaphan supported him (Jeremiah 26:23, 24). I think that one hurts, but what I can say is that the text puts Jeremiah's rescue right beside a person who stood with him. So speak the Word faithfully, and stand next to those who do.
